title: The request ran out of memory. What happens next?
description: Six flash cards on the PHP OOM bug class. Think through each prompt, flip for the explanation, and follow the state to cleanup.

completion.title: OOM is the trigger. Cleanup is the danger.
completion.description: A failure can interrupt initialization while state is reachable. If shutdown still handles that state as valid, cleanup can expose memory corruption. The PHP advisory documents RCE; these cards stay at the mechanism level.

cards.context: Before thinking about the bug, separate request memory from the machine’s total RAM.
cards.title: A per-request budget
cards.answer: PHP’s memory_limit caps memory used by one request. The server may still have free RAM when that request cannot get another allocation.

cards.prompt: How can state be both incomplete and dangerous?
cards.context: Picture initialization in progress when an allocation fails.
cards.title: Reachable does not mean ready
cards.answer: Some request state can become reachable before it is fully initialized. An out-of-memory exit at that moment can leave it invalid but still available to later code.

cards.prompt: After an early OOM exit, what part of the lifecycle matters?
cards.context: The failed allocation is only the trigger. Trace what happens after control leaves that context.
cards.title: Request shutdown
cards.answer: Shutdown may still process request state after initialization was interrupted. The allocation that fails does not have to be the allocation that created the unsafe state.

cards.prompt: What assumption can make cleanup unsafe?
cards.context: A structure is reachable, but initialization did not finish.
cards.title: Reachable is not valid
cards.answer: Cleanup can read or branch on state as though it were fully initialized. If that assumption is false, shutdown can consume invalid state and cause memory corruption.

cards.prompt: What does “the advisory documents RCE” tell us—and what does it not tell us?
cards.context: Keep the confirmed impact separate from a general claim about memory corruption.
cards.title: Documented impact, careful explanation
cards.answer: The advisory documents remote code execution for this vulnerability. Memory corruption does not automatically mean RCE in every bug, and this card deck does not reconstruct the exploit chain.

cards.prompt: At a high level, how does the patched OOM handling change the exit?
cards.context: This summary follows the advisory. It is not an independent patch review.
cards.title: Avoid the unsafe early exit
cards.answer: The advisory describes delayed soft OOM at the next VM safe point, plus immediate hard OOM termination at a higher threshold. The goal is to keep shutdown from seeing invalid state.
